title: Slow Cooker Corned Beef
metaDescription: Slow cooker corned beef with cabbage, carrots and potatoes — fork-tender after 8 hours with almost no hands-on work.
author: Laura Bennett
keywords: slow cooker corned beef, crockpot corned beef and cabbage, easy corned beef
ingredients: 3 lb corned beef brisket with spice packet

steps.name: Load the crockpot
steps.text: Place carrots, potatoes and onion in the bottom of the crockpot. Set the corned beef brisket on top, fat-side up, and sprinkle with the included spice packet.

steps.name: Add liquid
steps.text: Pour in beef broth or water until it comes about halfway up the sides of the meat. Add bay leaves.

steps.name: Cook
steps.text: Cover and cook on low for 7 hours.

steps.name: Add cabbage
steps.text: Nestle the cabbage wedges into the liquid around the meat. Cover and cook 1 more hour until the beef is fork-tender and cabbage is soft.

steps.name: Slice and serve
steps.text: Remove the beef and let rest 10 minutes, then slice against the grain. Serve with the vegetables and cabbage.

tips.question: Why add the cabbage later instead of at the start?
tips.answer: Cabbage cooks much faster than the tougher root vegetables and the brisket — adding it for just the last hour keeps it tender instead of turning to mush over the full 8-hour cook.

tips.question: Why slice against the grain?
tips.answer: Corned beef brisket has long muscle fibers — slicing across them shortens the fibers and makes each bite noticeably more tender than slicing with the grain.

tips.question: Can I use the spice packet if it seems small for the size of the meat?
tips.answer: Yes — the packets are portioned for the brisket they come with regardless of size; it's meant to season the cooking liquid, not coat the meat directly.

storyIntro: Corned beef rewards the same low-and-slow patience as a good pot roast — the crockpot breaks down the tough brisket into something that shreds apart with a fork.
Adding the cabbage only for the last hour is the one timing detail that keeps it from turning into mush by serving time.
storyNote: Hold the cabbage back until the final hour of cooking — added at the start alongside the tougher vegetables, it turns completely mushy well before the meat is done.
